cards.name: Directional Smooth
cards.summary: Edge-aware smoothing: CorelDRAW looks at neighbouring pixels of similar colour and smooths most along the direction they run, so flat areas and gradients get cleaner while outlines stay where they are. It reads as a light clean-up (less grain, blotchiness and dithering), not as a visible blur: on the soft PGD photo even Percentage 100 changed nothing visible, in a 1:1 crop too (mean 0.1 levels), so how much grain or dithering it removes is untested.
use_for: cleaning grain or JPEG blotches out of a low-quality client photo before it goes into a layout
evening out sky or skin gradients without softening the outlines around them
pre-cleaning a photo before Bitmaps > Quick Trace so fewer specks turn into shapes
avoid: Wanting a soft-focus or out-of-focus look: Effects > Blur > Gaussian Blur gives a real blur.
Stair-stepped edges on line art or a low-res logo: Effects > Blur > Jaggy Despeckle targets those.
Strong edge-preserving flattening (painted / plastic look) is beyond this effect: try Effects > Blur > Smart Blur at a high Amount, or Photoshop's Filter > Blur > Surface Blur.
This effect's scripted command string was not applied in a harvest test (the format is proven on other effects): check the bitmap after a scripted run.

cards.name: Feather
cards.summary: Softens the object's outer edge by fading it to transparency across a band Width wide, so a photo or shape melts into whatever sits behind it instead of ending on a hard border; the interior stays sharp. Mode picks the fall-off profile of that fade (Curved, Linear or Gaussian). The harvest audit showed the key working with no change in bitmap size, unlike Gaussian Blur which grows the bitmap.
use_for: photo dissolving softly into a poster or banner background
soft-edged cut-out of a portrait or product placed on a coloured panel
soft light patch or glow made from a feathered vector shape
blending two photos in a collage without a visible seam
avoid: The whole image should look soft, not just its edges: Effects > Blur > Gaussian Blur.
A rectangular photo feathers into a soft rectangle; for an oval fade, PowerClip it into an ellipse first or use Effects > Creative > Vignette.
Width over 2000 is accepted by the scripted path (8010 worked in the audit) but stay inside the dialog range 1-2000.
Over a white page the fade reads as a white haze around the object; judge it over the background it will really sit on.
A misspelt key is silently ignored: the audit's 'NoSuchKeyWidth' string returned without error and left the pixels unchanged.

params.name: Width
params.does: width of the faded band along the edge (logarithmic slider); wider = longer, softer fade into the background

params.name: Mode
params.does: fall-off profile of the fade from opaque to transparent: Curved (default), Linear or Gaussian; they differ in how quickly the edge drops away
params.typical: Curved; try Gaussian for the softest edge

pairs_with: Object/PowerClip/Place Inside Frame (shape the feather with an ellipse or custom frame)

cards.name: Gaussian Blur
cards.summary: The standard even blur: each pixel is averaged with its neighbours using a bell-shaped (Gaussian) weighting, so detail, type and hairlines soften into a haze; Radius sets how far the blur spreads. From a script even the dialog maximum Radius 250 gives only a light blur on a 1920 px photo: in a 1:1 crop hard edges spread over about 8-10 px and flat tones lift by about 5 levels (black 16 -> 22). The blur spills past the original edge, so the bitmap grows a little (the audit saw 1920x1080 become 1928x1088 at Radius 212.5).
use_for: out-of-focus backdrop behind poster or thumbnail headline type
frosted-glass panel: blurred copy of the photo PowerClipped into a rounded rectangle
glow base: blurred duplicate of a logo or shape under the sharp original
calming a busy photo so overlaid text stays readable
avoid: Removing grain while keeping edges: Effects > Blur > Smart Blur or Effects > Noise > Remove Noise.
Directional speed streaks: Effects > Blur > Motion Blur; spinning blur: Radial Blur; burst from the centre: Zoom.
Only the outline should soften: Effects > Blur > Feather.
Radius above 250 is accepted by the scripted path (1010 worked in the audit) but stay inside the dialog range 0.1-250.
The grown bitmap shifts the object's bounds by a few pixels; re-align after applying if it sits on a grid.
A misspelt key is not rejected: the audit's 'NoSuchKeyRadius' string still blurred and grew the bitmap with some other radius, with no error, so check the key spelling.

expecting the scripted Radius to act as pixels: the 2026-10 gallery render at Radius 150 only softened the type and hairlines of a 1920 px photo, and at Radius 250 a 1:1 crop showed edges spread over only 8-10 px (the audit saw the bitmap grow just 4 px a side at Radius 212); for a heavy scripted blur apply it several times or blur a downsampled copy (not tested)

params.name: Radius
params.does: blur radius (logarithmic slider, 0.1 steps; the harvest records no unit); larger = softer and wider spread
params.typical: near the default 5 for a light soften; on the harvest test photo Radius 2 and 40 differed only slightly (0.58 over 48 sampled pixels), so a clearly blurred backdrop needs roughly 100-250: judge it in the preview

pairs_with: Uniform Transparency (blurred glow under a sharp copy)
Effects/Sharpen/Unsharp Mask on the foreground copy

cards.name: Jaggy Despeckle
cards.summary: Spreads pixel colours inside a small Width x Height window (the 1:1 render shows an even, repeatable smear, no random speckle) (1-5; the harvest records no unit) to smooth stair-stepped, jagged edges and isolated specks, mainly on line art and other high-contrast images; the result is a light anti-aliased softening of hard edges, not a blur of the whole picture. On a soft photo it changes little; it shows mostly on crisp type and hairlines.
use_for: smoothing the jagged edges of a low-res logo or icon received as a bitmap
cleaning stair-stepping on enlarged scanned line art before tracing it
taking the hard pixel edge off a screenshot or pixel graphic placed in a print layout
avoid: A visible soft-focus look: Effects > Blur > Gaussian Blur.
Photo grain or sensor noise: Effects > Noise > Remove Noise or Effects > Blur > Smart Blur.
Heavy smoothing is not possible: Width and Height top out at 5.
A logo that must stay crisp at any size: retrace it as vectors (Bitmaps > Outline Trace) instead of despeckling the bitmap.
This effect's scripted command string was not applied in a harvest test (format proven on other effects); the bool is written as 1 / 0 like its harvested default, check the result.

cards.name: Low Pass
cards.summary: Strips out fine detail and sharp edges (the high-frequency part of the image) and keeps the broad tones and smooth gradients; at high Percentage and Radius the picture turns hazy and blurred. Percentage sets the strength and Radius (1-20) how large an area each pixel is evaluated over; the exact character next to Gaussian Blur was not measured by the harvest.
use_for: hazy, low-detail background plate behind type
removing fine texture or a halftone screen from a scan before tracing or posterising
the smooth tone layer of a frequency-separation style edit, paired with High Pass
avoid: Precise, large soft-focus control: Effects > Blur > Gaussian Blur (radius up to 250).
Radius stops at 20, so on a large bitmap the haze stays limited; scale down or use Gaussian Blur.
Edges must stay crisp: Effects > Blur > Smart Blur.
This effect's scripted command string was not applied in a harvest test (format proven on other effects): check the result.

cards.name: Motion Blur
cards.summary: Smears every pixel along one straight line to fake movement or camera shake: Distance sets the streak length, Direction its angle on a compass wheel, and Sampling how pixels beyond the image border are filled. The bitmap grows to hold the streaks (the harvest test went from 1930x1090 at Distance 5 to 2080x1240 at Distance 80).
use_for: speed streaks behind a car, bike or delivery promo
dynamic action background for a sports or sale poster
whoosh trail on a blurred duplicate of headline type
simulated panning shot on a product photo
avoid: Spinning motion: Effects > Blur > Radial Blur; burst from the centre: Effects > Blur > Zoom.
It blurs the subject too: to keep a sharp subject, blur a duplicate and put the sharp copy (PowerClipped to the subject) on top.
Use paper color can bring a paper-coloured (usually white) fringe into the streaks at the edges of a dark image; Sample nearest edge pixel avoids that.
Stay inside the dialog range Distance 1-999, Direction 0-360.

params.name: Distance
params.does: streak length in pixels (logarithmic slider); longer = faster-looking motion

params.name: Direction
params.does: angle of the streak in degrees, set on a compass wheel in 5-degree steps
params.typical: 0 or 90; confirm the orientation in the preview, the harvest did not record which way 0 points

params.name: Sampling
params.does: how pixels outside the image are treated while streaking: ignored, filled with the paper colour, or repeated from the nearest edge pixel
params.typical: Sample (nearest edge pixel) for photos that fill the frame

pairs_with: Object/PowerClip/Place Inside Frame (sharp subject over the blurred copy)

cards.name: Radial Blur
cards.summary: Circular (spin) blur around a centre point: pixels are smeared along arcs, so the middle stays fairly sharp and the outer parts swirl more and more; Amount sets the strength. That it spins rather than bursts outward comes from CorelDRAW's long-standing behaviour (the outward burst is the separate Zoom effect), not from the harvest; the harvest records no centre parameter, so there is no known scripted way to move the centre.
use_for: spinning wheel, fan, turntable or rotor
vortex or swirl background for a music or gaming poster
hypnotic, dizzy energy around a central subject
avoid: Outward speed burst toward the viewer: Effects > Blur > Zoom.
Straight-line movement: Effects > Blur > Motion Blur.
Amount above 100 is accepted by the scripted path (410 worked in the audit) but stay inside the dialog range 1-100.
An off-centre spin: the harvest has no centre key and does not record a centre control in the dialog; crop or PowerClip so the subject sits in the middle of the bitmap.
A misspelt key is not rejected: the audit's 'NoSuchKeyAmount' string still changed the pixels (7.79 from the original), with no error, so check the key spelling.

cards.name: Smart Blur
cards.summary: Edge-preserving blur: smooths low-contrast areas such as skin, sky, grain and noise while strong edges and outlines stay crisp, so the image looks cleaner or lightly airbrushed rather than out of focus. Its single setting is labelled Amount in the dialog but stored under the key Detail; the harvest did not measure its strength, so on an already soft photo the change may be modest even at 100.
use_for: skin smoothing on a portrait for a poster or hoarding
cleaning grain or sensor noise from a photo before print
flattening textures into cleaner areas before posterising or tracing
smoothing a sky gradient without softening the skyline
avoid: An out-of-focus backdrop: Effects > Blur > Gaussian Blur.
Pushed hard on faces it gives waxy, plastic skin; keep it moderate on people.
This effect's scripted command string was not applied in a harvest test (format proven on other effects): check the result.

a light smoothing pass before posterising or tracing
avoid: A visible blur: Effects > Blur > Gaussian Blur.
Stronger clean-up that still keeps edges: Effects > Blur > Smart Blur.
Taming over-sharpened edges specifically: Effects > Blur > Soften is aimed at that.
